page: Amazon Web Services m9g.large is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture featuring the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers two physical, dedicated cores with one thread per core (two vCPUs), paired with 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core). It includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration for AES. It operates without dedicated GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring remote storage solutions, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core efficiency alongside modest parallel throughput. The Neoverse-V3 architecture achieves high-tier single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2233.0, gzip compression at 36.54 GB/sec, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 17.3 GB/sec. Memory subsystems also demonstrate solid capacity handling, as evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2799.13 and uncached read throughput of 65.44 GB/sec. However, because the instance provides only two cores, total multi-threaded performance is restricted. This is reflected in lower relative scores across multi-core Geekbench (4111.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (34.1 GB/sec), and PassMark CPU score (2830.96).

In qualitative terms, the m9g.large offers an efficient compute-per-watt and memory profile typical of modern ARM-based deployments. Its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a resource distribution suitable for predictable enterprise applications without the operational overhead of hyperthreading contention. Tradeoffs include low multi-core aggregate compute ceiling, entry-level network baseline capacity, and the absence of bundled local storage.

This server type is suitable for moderate general-purpose workloads, including small-scale microservices, static web serving (measured at 7.64 GB/sec), caching tiers such as Redis (achieving 6.5 million SET operations per second), and standard application backends with limited concurrency demands.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration, accompanied by 8.0 GB of system memory, or 4.0 GB per core. It contains no onboard GPUs and relies on remote network storage, with local storage listed as None, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier single-threaded compute efficiency, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2233.0 and strong compression throughput, though multi-threaded capacity remains constrained by the two-core count. The configuration provides balanced memory and compute resources, making it appropriate for lightweight container orchestration, static web servers, Redis cache instances, and intermediate database operations.
